actor: Unidentified single operator (Gambit names no group; researchers told Bloomberg they do not believe a foreign government is involved)
impact: Per Gambit Security: at least nine Mexican government organizations breached, data exfiltrated from databases holding hundreds of millions of citizen records (including a claimed 195 million taxpayer records), hundreds of internal servers compromised, a live query service and a forged tax-certificate service operated on the stolen access, and a state government's virtualization infrastructure taken over. Initial reporting cited about 150 GB stolen. The federal tax authority denies any breach, and Bloomberg reported denials from two other listed victims.
mitigations: Gambit notes that many exploited weaknesses were addressable through standard controls (patching, credential rotation, network segmentation and endpoint detection) and urges organizations to address technical debt such as end-of-life systems that can no longer receive security updates.

Anthropic said it disrupted the activity and banned the associated accounts, and pointed to cyber-specific misuse probes in Claude Opus 4.6; OpenAI said its models refused the policy-violating attempts and it banned the adversary's accounts.
Gambit says affected organizations were notified with outside help including the Shadowserver Foundation, and that it delayed the full report at the parties' request to allow incident response.
name: Single operator used Claude Code and GPT-4.1 to breach Mexican government organizations (Dec 2025-Feb 2026)

summary: Gambit Security disclosed on 2026-02-25, in research first reported by Bloomberg, that a single unidentified operator used Anthropic's Claude Code and OpenAI's GPT-4.1 API as core operational tools in a campaign against Mexican public-sector organizations between late December 2025 and mid-February 2026. Gambit's full technical report (2026-04-10), based on forensic material recovered from three attacker servers, says at least nine federal, state and municipal government organizations were breached, including a municipal water utility, and that the operator exfiltrated databases holding hundreds of millions of citizen records and built a live query service into one agency's systems with a document-forgery service on top of it. Per Gambit, Claude Code generated and executed about 75 percent of remote command execution (5,317 AI-executed commands from 1,088 logged prompts across 34 sessions), working conversationally under the operator's direction through reconnaissance, exploit customization, privilege escalation, persistence and data extraction, while a custom tool sent harvested server data to GPT-4.1 to produce 2,597 analysis reports. Claude initially refused and asked for proof of authorization; the operator worked around it with a bug-bounty cover story and a pre-written playbook loaded into every session, and refusals recurred throughout. Gambit notes several victims were compromised manually and the forgery code was not written by Claude. Anthropic and OpenAI said they banned the accounts involved. Mexico's federal tax authority issued a statement on 2026-02-25 categorically denying any breach after reviewing its system logs, and Bloomberg reported that two other listed victims also denied being breached; Gambit's victim list has not been independently confirmed. Unit 42 later cited Gambit's report while tracking related activity against Latin American organizations as cluster CL-CRI-1131.
